entertainment.title: ‘Slick, Cheeky, Playful And a Little Provocative’: VASSY Serves Up ‘Dirty Martini’
entertainment.summary: For her next trick, VASSY unleashes “Dirty Martini,” a sassy, naughty nightcap with a shuffling beat and inner-city vibes.
entertainment.body:
Hits, history, kids, and Tomorrowland. If the year 2026 has been a blur for VASSY , that’s entirely fair.

The U.S.-based Australian singer and EDM star this year made her solo debut at Tomorrowland , became a mom, and made history when her single “Day N Night,” a collaboration with fellow Australian artist BUST-R, went to No. 1 on the ARIA Club Chart. With that feat, VASSY became just the sixth female artist to lead the tally. VASSY’s number went on to log four consecutive weeks at the summit.

For her next trick, VASSY unleashes “Dirty Martini” (via KMVMUSIC). Dropping Friday, Nov. 13 and featuring production by fellow DJ Aussie Oscar Jamo, “Dirty Martini” is all-sass, a naughty nightcap with a shuffling beat and inner-city vibes. Related Aria Vega Wins Best New Artist at the 2026 Latin Grammys: 'Dreams Know No Fear' On Winning First Latin Grammy, Camila Fernández Thanks Expectant Baby for 'Strength to be Here' 50 Cent Trolls Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Affair With 'P.I.M.P.' Music Video AI Deepfake: 'Jensen Don't Sweat It' Explore Vassy See latest videos, charts and news

The new tune “shows a different side of me — slick, cheeky, playful and a little provocative, compared to some of my more soulful records,” VASSY tells Billboard . “I love being able to express different sides of my personality through music. Sometimes it’s about having fun and making people dance.”

Earlier in the year, the Darwin native enjoyed a U.K. chart hit with “On Me,” her neo-disco-inspired collaboration with producer Mind Electric. “Creatively, I’m in such an exciting place,” she explains. “Being independent gives me the freedom to explore new sounds, take risks and, most importantly, have fun without feeling boxed in by expectations or numbers.”

VASSY is a trailblazer in the EDM world, a hitmaker with upwards of 3 billion career streams, six No. 1s on Billboard’s Dance Club Songs chart, an APRA Billions Award, and a slice of history by becoming the first female and first Australian to receive the EDMA Icon Award in 2023.

“What a year. Becoming a mum has been life-changing, and I’m still navigating the beautiful chaos of balancing mum life with artist life,” she recounts. The Tomorrowland experience was “pure magic and a real full-circle moment” for VASSY, who first performed there a decade earlier alongside Tiësto, where she hit “Secrets” for a massive gathering.

“2026 has been a pretty special ride,” VASSY reflects. “There’s plenty more new music and exciting collaborations.”

entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By Ted Danson: 'I Was Not Really Fully Emotionally Baked Until Shortly Before I Met...'
entertainment.summary: Cheers actor Ted Danson talks about his long marriage with his wife Mary Steenburgen and how he worked on himself before they got together.
entertainment.body:
Some of the best Ted Danson shows have been later on in his career, and his role as the hellish architect Michael in "The Good Place" shows just how much fun he can have with bizarre characters. In recent years, however, he's led Netflix's "A Man on the Inside" as retiree Charles Nieuwendyk, who helps out a private detective.

Like many great comedies, it's hilarious but also has a heartfelt streak baked into its story, as Nieuwendyk is still grieving the loss of his wife and lives a mundane life until he starts working for investigator Julie Kovalenko (Lilah Richcreek Estrada). Sadly, Netflix confirmed in September that " "A Man on the Inside" will end with Season 3 . To celebrate Danson's work on the series, here's his quote of the day.

Static Media "I was not really fully emotionally baked until shortly before I met Mary ... Thank God we didn't meet earlier."

Ted Danson spoke about his 30-plus-year marriage to Mary Steenburgen in an interview with People back in 2024. The "Cheers" star explained that during his 40s, he recognized that he needed to grow into more of an "emotionally mature, honest human being." Danson said that he doubts Steenburgen would've got into a relationship with him if he hadn't spent that time working on himself.

The pair had previously met during auditions for 1983's "Cross Creek," but Danson didn't land the role. They reconnected when they both worked on the 1994 adventure movie "Pontiac Moon." Clearly, Danson's personal development efforts paid off — they've been happily married since 1995.

Of course, personal development is quite a broad concept, and it can be different for everybody depending on their personality, life circumstances, or even their job. But at it's heart, it's about ensuring you can deal with everyday life alongside the difficulties of the modern world with a level head. There's no time limit on this kind of personal development, as Danson himself implied when he said that he was in his 40s before he had that realization.

entertainment.title: ‘Women and War’ Follows Four Ukrainians’ Journeys Towards Healing From Trauma (Exclusive IDFA Trailer)
entertainment.summary: "War does not end for these women when the weapons fall silent," highlights director Elwira Niewiera, whose doc about women going through long-term therapy premieres at IDFA in Amsterdam.
entertainment.body:
Four women in Ukraine who have survived Russia’s war. Four stories, including captivity, torture, sexual violence, times of hiding in dark basements, and the loss of loved ones. One shared journey – a journey toward healing. That is what the new documentary Women and War by Elwira Niewiera ( The Hamlet Syndrome , The Prince and the Dybbuk , The Domino Effect ) promises to take you on.

The film gets its world premiere on Sunday, Nov. 15 in the main competition of the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ), which runs through Nov. 22. Related Stories Movies 'Pop Pop' Dives Into Radicalization and Male Fragility in the Digital Age. Its Creator Says It's "More Topical Every Day" - and Urges Us to Join Hands. TV "Evil All Along": How Russell Brand Got Caught

Women and War follows the journeys of Olena, Yuliia, Iryna, and Lena, who survived Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. Over the course of a year, the doc shows them going through long-term therapy in the remote mountains of the country as they slowly begin to heal under the care of therapists and psychologists. And each of them must follow her own path toward recovery as they confront the lasting impact of trauma in the hope of regaiingn emotional and physical balance. Can they overcome their struggles and reclaim their lives?

“Women who have experienced violence during the war often continue to live in a constant state of fear, even after being released from captivity,” Niewiera says. “Many lose their sense of security, their trust in others and their connection to their own bodies. Because the body is often the only witness to what happened to them, the mind tries to disconnect from it, leaving them emotionally and physically numb.” She adds: “The war does not end for these women when the weapons fall silent. It continues to shape their thoughts, their bodies and their everyday lives. Yet violence against women in conflict is still too often overlooked, even as rape and torture are deliberately used to break individuals and destabilise entire communities.”

She recalls seeing the women’s difficulties reconnecting with their emotions. “Some struggled to express sadness, anger or even joy,” highlights the director. “In therapy, I watched their feelings slowly returning, as they learned to give them a voice. I wanted the film to look beyond trauma and show their courage, strength and the small steps they take towards healing. Alongside the pain, there is warmth and empathy. These women are not defined by what they have endured, but also by their determination to reclaim their lives.”

entertainment.title: Lorde-Backed Album-Focused Music Platform Lume Expands Into Australia
entertainment.summary: In a digital world where singles make so much of the noise, New Zealand-based Lume is a music service with a point of difference.
entertainment.body:
AUCKLAND, New Zealand — Lume is crossing the ditch. The innovative New Zealand-based, album-focused music app expands into Australia with a new round of artist releases, official chart status, and a key addition to the team.

Just days after winning the 2026 Australian Music Prize for her sophomore album , Looking For People to Unfollow , Ecca Vandal leads a cast of artists dropping enhanced versions of their LPs on the service. Fellow Aussie acts Ocean Alley, DZ Deathrays, The Rubens, The Tullamarines and others today (Nov. 13) release albums through the platform, which are available to purchase. Related CL Signs With THEBLACKLABEL, Reuniting With Longtime Producer Teddy For 'Full Circle' Moment Jeff Benjamin

In a digital world where singles — the shorter, the better — make so much of the noise, Lume is a music service with a point of difference. Co-founded by NZ music and media professionals Duncan Greive, Tim Harper, Sacha Judd , and Justin Warren, the startup is a hive for album afficionados. A place for fans and superfans. With some LPs, customers can access exclusive video, audio and photography, for what Greive pitches as “the most complete and immersive version of an album available anywhere.”

Operating with a direct-to-fan ownership model instead of a streaming subscription plan, Lume shells out 80% of revenue directly to artists and rightsholders, reps say.

With that mission, Lume has secured seed investment from a group including including Lorde (real name: Ella Yelich-O’Connor), Substack co-founder Hamish McKenzie and Letterboxd’s co-founder and CTO Karl von Randow. “I think Lume is really smart,” remarks Yellich-O’Connor in a statement. “It’s a missing piece in the puzzle of modern album-sharing, giving artists an opportunity for deep intimacy with their core listeners while dictating what their work is truly worth.”

The platform was founded in 2025, launched in July 2026, and this week expands into neighboring Australia. Lume does so after striking an agreement with Brisbane, Australia-based distributor G.Y.R.O., and its inventory is chart eligible with trade body ARIA, joining certification from its New Zealand counterpart RMNZ.

As Lume muscles up, the business launches its own Substack. On Lume will explore both the artists and the albums featured on the platform, and cover key stories in music, and is led by new recruit Conor Lochrie, the renowned music journalist and former Rolling Stone AU/NZ deputy editor.

entertainment.title: ‘Heartland’ Review: Jessica Chastain Does Sturdy Work as a Hard-Edged Former Country Music Star Saddled With a Thriller in Name Only
entertainment.summary: Writer-director Shana Feste ('Country Strong') dives into Nashville’s sleazy underbelly in a mystery built on dark secrets, also starring Garrett Hedlund and country singer Carter Faith.
entertainment.body:
Imagine an episode of ABC’s Nashville written by Taylor Sheridan, but despite a load of fun stuff — a disappearance, a murder plot, festering secrets, shady talent management, an obsessive stalker, a shootout, cowboy boots and Stetsons — it barely has a pulse. Writer-director Shana Feste returns to the milieu of her instantly forgotten 2010 Gwyneth Paltrow vehicle Country Strong , this time going several shades darker. But even after watching the suspense-free Netflix original for two hours, I had to refer to the press notes to learn that it’s a “gritty neo-noir thriller.” Sure, Jan. Related Stories TV 'Below' Star Rohan Campbell on Finding That Newfoundland Accent and Losing Himself in Roles TV Gang Dong-won, Kim Go-eun to Lead Netflix's Period Romance-Action Drama 'The Twilight Between Us'

Jessica Chastain stars as Misty Jones, a country music legend who fled Nashville 20 years earlier, leaving a failed marriage, a career downturn and a lot of bad press behind her. We know she’s been bruised and hardened by experience because she wears no makeup, stringy hair and ratty tank tops, living as a recluse on a remote Georgia pecan farm with her decrepit dogs. She also helpfully pops on a video of an old TV interview at one point, which should be labeled “exposition.” Heartland The Bottom Line Dullsville. Release date : Friday, Nov. 13 Cast : Jessica Chastain, Garrett Hedlund, Carter Faith, Ross Lynch, Paul Sparks, Jennifer Nettles, John Hawkes, Hill Harper, Norbert Leo Butz, Wynn Everett Director-screenwriter : Shana Feste Rated R, 1 hour 53 minutes

Misty interrupts her life of boozing and bar pickups when her brother Donny (Paul Sparks) calls asking for her help following the disappearance of his 22-year-old daughter Charlie Hart (rising country star Carter Faith in a passable acting debut). Charlie has become a significant music figure in a relatively short time, pumping out 10 albums and touring nonstop. Even though she has gone AWOL and resurfaced in the past — showing up late or not at all for concerts and disappointing her fans — Donny is convinced she’s in trouble after being unable to reach her for three days. With his wife undergoing cancer treatment, Donny can’t go to Nashville to look for Charlie, so he convinces her abrasive estranged aunt to go instead.

Even before Misty arrives back in Music City, Donny steers her toward two suspects — Jared Granger (JP Edwards), a sicko stalker whose attentions prompted Charlie to take out a restraining order; and her boyfriend Jace Jacobs (Ross Lynch), a cocky young country rocker whose romantic duets with Charlie tell a different story to their real relationship. Neither Donny nor Misty buys the statement of Charlie’s manager Kelly (Wynn Everett) that she’s merely taking a break on a songwriting retreat.

entertainment.title: Lisa’s ‘Viva La Lisa’ Las Vegas Residency Setlist: Every Song From Night 1
entertainment.summary: Lisa performed all six songs from her new EP, "Press Play," while making history on the Las Vegas Strip.
entertainment.body:
Lisa wrote a new chapter in her career Thursday night (Nov. 12), becoming the first K-pop artist to headline a Las Vegas residency as she kicked off “Viva La Lisa” at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace.

Packed with fire, leather and lingerie moments, the BLACKPINK rapper, singer and dancer brought her solo catalog to the Strip for the first of six performances scheduled through Nov. 29. Originally announced as a four-show engagement, the production expanded after the initial dates sold out in less than 10 minutes. Additional performances are scheduled for Nov. 13-14 and 27-29.

Divided into five chapters, the 90-minute, perfectly choreographed “Viva La Lisa” draws heavily from her debut solo album, Alter Ego , released in February 2025, while putting her new six-track EP, Press Play , front and center.

Released Oct. 23, the project is represented in its entirety, from the cinematic “Tarantino,” which opens the show, to “SaWaDiKa,” the Thai-inspired single that closes the evening. The remaining four tracks—“V12,” “Cobra,” “Cut U Off,” and “Sweat”—are sprinkled throughout.

The setlist embraces all the major hits from her still-new but momentous K-pop culture run, including “Money,” her breakout solo single from 2021, and “Rockstar,” along with collaborations “New Woman,” featuring Rosalía, and “Born Again,” with Doja Cat and Raye.

Her first solo album, Alter Ego , debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200, establishing her career outside BLACKPINK. Performing in Vegas signifies another milestone for the Thai-born performer, who made her solo Coachella debut in 2025 and expanded into acting with HBO’s The White Lotus .

entertainment.title: Dolly Parton Heals the Soul on Final Recording, ‘Torn,’ a Duet With Bono on U2’s New Album
entertainment.summary: The posthumous song appears on the band’s 16th album, Carnaval de Luz , out now
entertainment.body:
For those missing Dolly Parton (and there are many), the country great’s final recording may feel like a revelation.

On Friday, U2 released their 16th studio album, Carnaval de Luz , which saves the best for last: “Torn,” a duet between frontman Bono and Parton. The singer, who died in August at age 80, recorded her part in June, and shares writing credits for the song with the band and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid. ”When she got ill,” Bono told Rolling Stone for U2’s recent cover story , “she got out of her bed to sing this song. And you can hear that. And I can’t even listen to it now.”

The song opens with faint voices in the background over a steady heartbeat and soon, Parton’s distinct vibrato fills every lyric. At first, a story about someone deciding between over two lovers appears to be unfolding, until the chorus with Bono reveals a broader division: “Torn apart these loving hearts that beat and break the same/We share a house divided and the blood that fills our veins/Brothers turn to strangers and sons deny their name.” On a verse, Parton sings, “Nothing hurts a mother more than a family at war.”

Bono initially pursued Parton for a still-in-progress Irish-roots side project and while he played her a few sketches over the phone, he recalled her replying, “That’s a little too Irish.” Bono said she eventually sent a song of her own, titled “Torn.”

While Parton originally wrote it around tale of a woman trying to choose between two men, Bono and McDaid rewrote the lyrics around a mother watching her family split apart. “You name the location,” Bono said when discussing the tensions the song evokes, “but everyone knows what it is … People say in the U.S. now, people are scared to go into Thanksgiving.”

entertainment.title: All the 2026 Latin Grammys Performances, Ranked
entertainment.summary: Which artists stood out at this year's ceremony?
entertainment.body:
The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards brought together some of the biggest names in Latin music for a night celebrating the sounds, stories and artists shaping the global music landscape. Presented Thursday (Nov. 12) at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, the 27th annual ceremony featured a star-studded lineup spanning reggaetón, música mexicana, salsa, pop, rock and beyond, with performances that showcased the genre’s ever-expanding reach.

Hosted by Roselyn Sánchez, the three-hour telecast welcomed a mix of established icons and rising stars, including Karol G, Rosalía, Daddy Yankee, Juanes, Carín León, Anitta, Feid, Milo J, Mon Laferte, Bad Gyal and Nathy Peluso, among many others. The evening also paid tribute to two towering figures in Latin music: the late salsa legend Willie Colón, whose groundbreaking contributions helped define the New York salsa movement, and the late Mexican songwriting icon José Alfredo Jiménez, honored in celebration of the centennial of his birth.

Beyond the marquee names, the award ceremony reflected the breadth of contemporary Latin music, bringing together artists from across generations, countries and musical traditions. From the enduring influence of tropical rhythms to the continued evolution of urbano and the international rise of música mexicana, the lineup offered a snapshot of a musical landscape that continues to defy expectations.

If you want to see a complete list of the winners , we got you. If you want to read what happened inside the Person of the Year event, who this year is Daddy Yankee, head here . But if you want to know which performances left the strongest impression, check out our list below, ranked.

Three distinctive voices from across Latin America came together for a performance that had more musical promise than memorable moments. Carín León, sporting his signature wide-brimmed hat, opened with “Desde Que Te Tengo,” bringing his unmistakable nasal twang to the stage. Juanes, looking effortlessly cool in a leather jacket, delivered a polished vocal performance on “Humano,” joined by Mexican singer-songwriter Vivir Quintana, whose deep vibrato, striking streak of white hair and all-black ensemble made her a compelling presence. The stripped-down instrumentation gave each artist room to shine, though the collaboration never quite developed the chemistry or dramatic momentum needed to stand out in such a competitive lineup.

entertainment.title: ‘Pop Pop’ Dives Into Radicalization and Male Fragility in the Digital Age. Its Creator Says It’s “More Topical Every Day” – and Urges Us to Join Hands.
entertainment.summary: Writer-director Dylan Stephen Levers' debut feature is a cinematic parable, premiering at Tallinn, that was partly shot at alt-right marches and is full of memes and indie spirit.
entertainment.body:
U.S. filmmaker Dylan Stephen Levers’ ( this is a film about tom and maddy ) debut feature, Pop Pop , is a cinematic parable that hits us not only with unusual and memorable visuals and sounds, but also hits us hard with all sorts of queasiness-inducing questions for our age of virality, digital nihilism, the manosphere and radicalization.

In true independent spirit and pop art fashion, the movie is a cinematic mash-up of meme culture, trips into cyberspace and alt-right protests that explores toxic masculinity, cancel culture and a sea of identity crises without any apparent lifeboats. Related Stories TV "Evil All Along": How Russell Brand Got Caught Business Around 10-15 Percent of SAG-AFTRA Membership Wants AI Blocked, CEO Tells Web Summit

Pop Pop gets its world premiere on Sunday during the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia. And it only seems fitting that it debuts in the fest’s Rebels With a Cause Competition program.

Written and directed by Levers, Pop Pop stars Cashton Tate Rehklau, Trevor Jonathan Lown and Lena Kutscher, along with Austin Davis, Djuna Knight, Kevin Confoy and Marta Kotzien. Rehklau and Lown are Dustin and Dibz, best friends who survived their senior year of college and now share an apartment in New York and an Internet series. But where do they go from here? Well, they end up taking very different paths.

Dustin becomes immersed in an increasingly radical worldview, focusing on attracting attention and a following via provocative online posts. Dibz finds meaning in social justice activism and his first crush on a man, forcing him to reconsider his identity. The film mixes fictional scenes with footage shot during real-life protests and psychedelic animations that take the audience into the digital world, including the manosphere.

Pop Pop is a Body by Lulz Films production, co-produced by Grease NYC. The cinematographer is Consuelo Althouse, while Josh Coll handled editing. W. Ian Ross, Levers and Althouse produced Pop Pop , with Stefanie Abel Horowitz, Josh Bierne-Golden and Erin Magill serving as executive producers.

In a director’s statement, Levers says he began writing Pop Pop in 2016, “as angry white men were gathering online, sharing extremist ideas about immigrants, Islam, women, and the supposed destruction of the ‘white race.’ What the media dismissed as a fringe movement soon became a significant political force.”

The British act’s long-time collaborator and producer Nile Rodgers has paid tribute to Taylor, now 66, as the heartbeat of the legendary new wave band.

“I wish Roger Taylor love, happiness and a peaceful life,” he writes in a social post. “I love Duran Duran. “They’re my longest musical relationship. This year we shared a historical tour with them and our relationship grew even stronger. We’ll always be connected for life.”

Taylor, who is no relation to the band’s founding bass player John Taylor and guitarist Andy Taylor, was behind the kit in two outstanding Duran Duran eras.

Lightyears before Hollywood’s obsession with beauty biohacking , Keren Bartov was already using medical-grade, high-tech skin care tools to bring glow-from-within radiance to stars’ visages. Her results were most recently seen on clients Cate Blanchett, Elizabeth Debicki and Mikey Madison, who visited the celebrity facialist ’s Notting Hill studio for bespoke facials ahead of the annual Harper’s Bazaar Women of the Year Awards in London on Nov. 5.

The 47-year-old aesthetician also saved A-listers from a cross-Atlantic trip by popping up in LA with her suite of skin-plumping, jawline-snatching devices and her own Keren Bartov Advanced Skin Care serums and creams ahead of the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show and Academy Museum Gala last month. She also prepped Kim Kardashian’s skin for her 46th birthday party, and also works with Beyonce and mom Tina Knowles, Julia Roberts, Michelle Monaghan, Eiza Gonzalez, Anya Taylor-Joy and Olivia Wilde, to name just a handful. “Before a major event, my goal is for the skin to look its absolute best while remaining calm, balanced and refreshed. The last thing I want is to cause irritation or an unexpected reaction right before a red carpet,” notes Bartov. “I often combine technologies that help improve the appearance of firmness and texture with lymphatic drainage, gentle enzymatic exfoliation and skin care that delivers hydration and radiance.”

In fact, the U.K.-based skin expert has an arsenal of more than 50 technologies — in which she’s invested millions of dollars to ensure only the most state-of-the-art facials — “but the number itself isn’t what matters. I never introduce a technology or ingredient simply because it’s new or everyone is talking about it. For me, innovation has to be backed by science, safety and meaningful results.”

The duet between Dolly and U2 frontman Bono is the closing song on Carnaval De Luz (which translates to “Carnival of Light”), the Irish rock band’s sixteenth and latest studio album. Co-written by U2, Parton and Snow Patrol ‘s Johnny McDaid , “Torn” is the country great’s last recorded vocal performance , and it connects the full 24-track deluxe version of the project, followed in sequence by the surprise-release EPs Days of Ash and Easter Lily , as a double album.

Dolly pulls it together, to create a spiritual whole. “You sense a border crossing,” Bono remarks in a statement. “And so you move from the south into the north, and you have Dolly Parton singing to you as you cross the border.”

entertainment.summary: Janet Jackson also presented Daddy Yankee with the person of the year honor.
entertainment.body:
Spanish singer Rosalía took home the top prize of album of the year at the 2026 Latin Grammys on Thursday night for her 2025 album Lux .

She opened the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards, live from Sin City, with an emotive medley of her Lux tracks “La Rumba Del Perdón,” “La Perla” and “Dios Es Un Stalker,” joined by angelic dancers ornamented with halos atop a stage meant to look like heavenly clouds.

It was a reminder of the expansiveness of her album: an offbeat, full-hearted embrace of her classical training through huge orchestral movements, inspired by the lives of female saints. Related Stories TV How to Stream the 2026 Latin Grammys Online Movies 'Wet,' Starring Connor Storrie, Rebecca Ferguson and Odessa A'zion, Acquired by Lionsgate

Her “La Perla” also won song of the year, and during her speech, she thanked Mexico and invited her collaborators on the song, the American urban sierreño trio Yahritza Y Su Esencia, to join her on stage.

Daddy Yankee , the 2026 Latin Grammy Awards’ person of the year and first Latin urbano artist to receive the honor, ripped through his biggest hits an hour into Thursday’s award show, treating the stage like a stadium floor.

It was one for the history books: There were outfit changes, set changes and his native Puerto Rico always at the forefront as he ran through “Ella Me Levantó,” “Con Calma,” “BOTZ,” “Despacito,” “Lo Que Pasó, Pasó,” “Sonríele,” “Rompe,” “Pokito” and, of course, “Gasolina” — joined by Bizarrap, Bad Gyal, Feid, Jay Wheeler, French Montana, LL Cool J and Diljit Dosanjh.

When it came time for Daddy Yankee to receive his honor, it was delivered to him by Janet Jackson “with admiration and respect,” as she said in her speech. When he accepted the award, he concluded by saying “Puerto Rico, recuerda. … Puerto Rico no es pequeño. Pequeño el mapa.” In English: “Puerto Rico, remember. … Puerto Rico is not small. The map is small.”

The award show took place live from Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena. It aired live on Univision, UniMás, Galavisión and ViX and hosted by actor, producer and musician Roselyn Sánchez.

She ended by honoring how her mother raised her. “Thanks, mama, for making me this way. I’m going to bring this Grammy to your house. I don’t know if another one is going to fit in your house, but I’ll bring it to you anyways and see if you make room.You always find a way for anything,” she said.

What began as a simple visit to check on her new birth-trauma pal Corrie quickly turned into a living nightmare when the expectant mother began experiencing stomach pains. Not only was Corrie in labor, but the umbilical cord was cutting off her baby's oxygen supply.

Given the PTSD she's still fighting to overcome, this was already a lot for Jo to handle — and it was about to get so much worse. During the ambulance ride to the hospital, Corrie's uterus began to rupture, forcing Jo to perform an emergency C-section en route to Grey Sloan. When the ambulance finally arrived, the image of Jo stepping out, covered in blood with the baby in her arms, was frankly haunting.

Fortunately, this story has a happy ending on all fronts. Not only did Corrie and the baby survive the ordeal, but Corrie's kind words to Jo about her fearlessness in the face of danger, and the comfort and strength she provides to her patients, inspired Jo to rethink a life outside of medicine .

"Maybe this thing I thought was a weakness is actually a strength," Jo told Webber, who wasn't thrilled about Jo practicing medicine in his hospital when she wasn't technically an OBGYN. "That's the best news I've heard all day," he said when she asked to return full-time, and we fully agree.

Actually, remember when we said everybody in this story got a happy ending? That's not entirely true, at least not for Link. Still concealing his obvious pill problem, Jo's husband got his fake stories mixed up this week, and Amelia — who knows a thing or two about battling addiction — is beginning to recognize the signs.

ABC Meanwhile, Kwan's reunion with his father — as teased in the final moments of last week's episode — went even worse than we expected. After all, he left home when Kwan was just four years old, so what could have changed since then? Two words, apparently: "I'm. Dying."

entertainment.body: A measles outbreak on Grey's Anatomy led to a main character revealing their chronic illness diagnosis — and temporarily leaving the hospital. During the Thursday, November 12, episode of the hit ABC series, Wes (Trevor Jackson) and Simone (Alexis Floyd) were at odds after she told him her ex-boyfriend Lucas (Niko Terho) — whom she recently hooked up with — was moving into the same house as her. The fictional couple were also working on the same medical case, which involved a patient with a mysterious rash that turned out to be measles. Wes ran out of the hospital, a reaction Simone thought stemmed from their fight. Instead, Wes revealed he had CVID (Common Variable Immunodeficiency) and the condition prevented him from being able to get vaccinated. His body does not produce enough antibodies to fight off germs effectively, so he had to leave the hospital for 28 days while they waited to see if he would develop symptoms. Elsewhere in the episode, Jo (Camilla Luddington) delivered friend Corrie's (Sarah Levy) baby in the back of an ambulance after major complications. Instead of being triggered by the procedure, Jo realized she wanted to return to work. Amelia (Caterina Scorsone), meanwhile, was starting to pick up on signs that Link (Chris Carmack) was addicted to the pain pills he prescribed for himself. Kwan (Harry Shum Jr.) faced his own issues when his dad arrived at the hospital to allegedly reconnect amid his terminal cancer diagnosis. Kwan initially believed his father, who was absent all his life, but with Jules' (Adelaide Kane) help, he realized his dad was trying to manipulate him into donating his bone marrow. Cracks also began to emerge in Ben (Jason George) and Miranda's (Chandra Wilson) marriage. Grey’s Anatomy has had its fair share of shakeups this season with an even more limited number of episodes. The medical drama previously had as many as 27 episodes per season, but this year, there are only 13. Despite the major changes, executive producer Meg Marinis is holding out hope that some former cast members might find a way to return this season. "I hope so! We love bringing former cast [members] back when they’re available and it makes sense story-wise," she told The Hollywood Reporter in October. entertainment.summary: Western fans looking for their next weekend binge should look no further than Emily Blunt's incredible and highly underrated miniseries.
entertainment.body:
Diego Lopez Calvin/Drama Republic/BBC/Amazon Studios Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Viewers on the hunt for an engrossing Western revenge thriller should look no further than the 2022 Prime Video limited series "The English," starring Emily Blunt.

Set in the late 19th century, the story centers on English aristocrat Lady Cornelia Locke (Blunt) — who embarks on a quest to find the man she blames for the death of her son. Along the way, she meets a Native American former army scout named Eli Whipp (Chaske Spencer), who has his own grievance regarding land owed to him. The unlikely duo encounters friends, foes, and plenty of peril as they make their way across Middle America.

While not based on a true story, the show's slow-burn narrative examines the racism, violence, and greed of the late 19th century with unflinching brutality. Scoring an 84% among critics and general audiences on Rotten Tomatoes, "The English" earned heaps of praise for its gorgeous visuals and superb acting performances. Plus, considering that "The English" is only six episodes long, it's a perfect series to binge over a weekend or holiday break.

Diego Lopez Calvin/Prime Video "The English" was Emily Blunt's first live-action TV appearance since she starred in the miniseries "Empire" back in 2005. Seventeen years later, Blunt traded the Roman Empire TV show about Julius Caesar for the gritty atmosphere of the American West, additionally serving as an executive producer on "The English". Characters typical of the Western genre can grow stale, though according to Blunt, "The English" writer and director Hugo Blick crafted Cornelia Locke as a unique outsider that the star was thrilled to discover.

"She's the most alive character I've ever read on a page," Blunt told Deadline . "She was so spontaneous and free and really unpredictable. She was so odd in some ways. Hugo's writing doesn't follow the rules and this character doesn't follow any archetype or character you've read before. But then you realize, oh, no, that's real life, that's what people are like."

Barker has previously shared insight into a past opioid addiction he developed over his lifelong fear of flying.

“My friends knew how much I dreaded being on planes, and one of them gave me a pill to help with my anxiety,” he said in his “Louder Than Fear” documentary.

The rocker said he went from taking just one or two OxyContin-type painkillers prior to flying to “having to be on them” or else he “couldn’t even function.”

entertainment.title: Law & Order: SVU Boss On The State Of Benson And Stabler's Relationship After The Emotionally Charged 600th Episode
entertainment.summary: Executive producer Michele Fazekas walks us through some of Benson and Stabler's toughest moments from the milestone outing.
entertainment.body:
Courtesy of NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Warning: This post contains spoilers from the 600th episode of "Law & Order: SVU," which aired Thursday. Please proceed accordingly.

Big "Law & Order: SVU" milestone, even bigger emotions stirred up between two former partners.

Thursday's episode of the NBC procedural found Det. Elliot Stabler (Chris Meloni) returning to the precinct to work with his longtime colleague Capt. Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) on a case they got wrong the first time around, nearly 30 years before.

As the pair reinvestigated the murder of a young nun, they inadvertently opened the Pandora's Box that started to fill the moment they were paired up back in the day. Translation: They had some really tough conversations about who they are now (and who they were then), a process showrunner Michele Fazekas tells TVLine was "cathartic" and indicative of the depth of the long-standing relationship between the characters.

Read on for lots more of what Fazekas had to say, including whether or not we should expect to see Stabler again in Season 28.

TVLINE | Personally, I love Stabler and Benson together. It was surprising to me that they haven't spoken since Cragen's wake. Talk to me about the decision to have them not have really any kind of interaction between then and now. MICHELE FAZEKAS | Well, I wanted to locate Stabler emotionally — it's where he is right now. I also wanted to have something really easily accessible for people who didn't watch "Law & Order: Organized Crime." So if you never watched "Organized Crime," that's fine. All you need to know is: His brother got killed, his mother has dementia, and he's kind of messed up right now. And I really liked bookending it with "We haven't spoken in 18 months" and he's been sort of not working to "You want to go to Arizona?"

TVLINE | I will say: the biggest of red flags. Like, no one needs to be with this man right now. This man needs to sort himself out. By the way, you've sort of exactly tagged what I feel, which is: He does need to sort himself out. He also knows what her answer is going to be to that question. He asks it, and the question in and of itself is what he wanted out there. He's not expecting her to say yes, but he wants her to know that he wants that.

And listen, I've said this before: I do think they love each other, and I think their love transcends a sexual relationship. That they deeply care about each other. And he's not ready. That's what I also wanted to show in this episode, because as much as I wanted to do a classic Benson-Stabler episode, our lead is Capt. Benson. And her story here is, she has really evolved from what she was 28, 29 years ago. And Stabler still has some work to do, and he knows that.

Law & Order: SVU reached a huge milestone Thursday: 600 episodes, a number that only two scripted primetime shows have ever hit before. The cast and crew celebrated with a cake on set during filming and a dinner afterward — and then went back to work. Six hundred episodes is an extremely rare feat for a scripted series ( The Simpsons and Gunsmoke are the only ones with more), but Thursday’s episode was also the sixth of season 28; 15 more are still to come. “That’s just doing television,” showrunner Michele Fazekas told The Hollywood Reporter . “It’s our 600th episode, but it’s also just an episode within 21 episodes [this season]. You’re working on five episodes at the same time at any given moment — you’re in prep on some episodes, you’re writing on some episodes, you’re in post on some episodes. Nothing changed in that regard.”

Titled “Obedience,” the 600th episode brings Elliot Stabler ( Christopher Meloni ) back to the Special Victims Unit after jury consultant Gwen Sharpe (J. Smith-Cameron, who also appeared in the season premiere) convinces Benson ( Mariska Hargitay ) to take another look at an old case. Gwen is convinced the man in prison for the crime, the rape and murder of a young nun in 1998, is innocent.

Stabler is reluctant to revisit the case — with good reason, it turns out. He failed to follow a couple of leads that could have pointed to the real culprit, a now-retired priest who led mass at the convent where the victim lived. He also cut Benson out of the interrogation in the case, which she went along with at the time because she was new to the squad. The case stirs up complicated feelings in the former partners; when Stabler asks Benson why she’s so interested in digging up the case, she retorts, “Why aren’t you?”

He eventually agrees to work with her, and the pair head upstate to question people who knew the victim (most notably, guest stars Laura Innes and Kathleen Chalfant) and track down the priest.

Fazekas, who wrote the episode (Brenna Malloy directed), said she wanted to give the 600th show the feel of “an old school Benson and Stabler episode” while also looking at the people they have become in the years since. To that end, the episode’s final scenes will give viewers plenty to discuss.

Elliot Stabler (Chris Meloni) are in rougher shape than we've seen in quite some time as the landmark 600th episode of "Law & Order: SVU" gets underway, and revisiting an old case from early in their partnership certainly doesn't help smooth things over.

Even if you're not into the "EO" of it all, the hour is a meaty one: The partners (and Liv's squad) reinvestigate the murder of a young nun and wind up uncovering a deeper, darker story of misplaced guilt and ruined lives. And there are a couple of excellent guest spots in the offing, as well.

Gwen ( J. Smith-Cameron ) corners Olivia outside of work and asks for her thoughts on an old case. As the pair walk the Highline, Gwen explains that she's been getting letters for years about a man who was incarcerated in 1998, but he maintains he's not guilty. Now that she's finally taken a look at the claim, she has questions. Liv agrees to help if she can, and that's when Gwen drops her bomb: It's the murder of Claire Sobel, a nun; at the mention of the name, Benson's face hardens. "Are you kidding me right now?" she asks, immediately defensive.

Gwen asks Benson to go through the case with her "one last time," mentioning in passing that "your old partner, he hasn't returned my calls."

entertainment.summary: Travis Barker's health scare has led him to dump weed. The Blink-182 drummer said he stopped smoking marijuana after receiving a troubling diagnosis. "I only quit because I got diagnosed with...
entertainment.body:
The Blink-182 drummer said he stopped smoking marijuana after receiving a troubling diagnosis.

"I only quit because I got diagnosed with precancer of the esophagus," Barker shared on the Nov. 11 episode of the Big Bro with Kid Cudi podcast. "I loved blunts and I would smoke too much."

In fact, the 50-year-old—who shares 3-year-old son Rocky Barker with wife Kourtney Kardashian , as well as kids Alabama Barker , 20, Landon Barker , 23, and stepdaughter Atiana de la Hoya , 27, with ex Shanna Moakler —said he "would have never stopped" until his doctor told him that it was a "serious" case.

"He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--k around. You’ve got to stop smoking,’” Barker recounted, recalling how he was smoking 10 to 15 blunts a day at the time. "I thought I could be like Willie Nelson and smoke to the day I die."

Still, the "Dumpweed" rocker thinks about lighting up "all the time."

However, Barker has since channeled that craving into a healthier habit: running .

"I've found even however many years later now, 20 years later, couple miles a day keeps the demons away," he continued. "My running started getting bigger and more important to me than smoking."

The "All the Small Things" musician noted that jogging—which he took up following his 2008 near-fatal plane crash —also played a large part in helping him overcome his addiction to prescription painkillers and opioids.

sports.title: Bruce Arians says he wants to be a head coach in the NFL next season
sports.summary: Bruce Arians is thinking about coming out of retirement.
sports.body:
Arians told Jordan Schultz that when he announced his retirement from the Buccaneers in March of 2022, it was because of health problems that have since been resolved, and he now wants to coach again.

“I had torn my Achilles early in that season, and I was wearing these prosthetic high heels, and it threw my back out, and I couldn’t stand on the sideline for four hours anymore without a lot of pain,” Arians said. “I was also monitoring an aneurysm on my heart, so I had some health issues. We did everything we thought we could do in Tampa after winning the Super Bowl, trying to get two, and then it was time to give it to Todd [Bowles]. Now that I’m all healthy again, I got the itch again. So, we’ll see.”

If Arians does come back next year, he’ll be the oldest head coach in NFL history. That distinction currently belongs to Pete Carroll, who was 74 when he coached the Raiders last season. Arians will turn 75 next season.

Arians’ first retirement announcement came from the Steelers after they did not renew his contract as their offensive coordinator following the 2011 season, but Arians later said he was forced out and didn’t want to retire. He then took a job as offensive coordinator of the Colts in 2012, and was their interim head coach for most of that season while Chuck Pagano battled leukemia. Arians coached so well that he was named the NFL’s Coach of the Year.

Once Pagano returned to the Colts, Arians became head coach of the Cardinals, and he won a second Coach of the Year award. He announced his retirement following the 2017 season, after five years as head coach of the Cardinals.

But in 2019 he came out of retirement to become head coach of the Buccaneers. He won a Super Bowl in Tampa Bay, then retired after three seasons. Arians thought that was it, but he said that his son is now coaching high school football, and in talking to his son about the job he realized how much he misses it himself.

“Another fire got lit,” Arians said. “I had no desire to go back, and I was still fighting some health issues, but now after the open heart surgery I’ve got so much more energy, it’s amazing.”

Arians may find, like Bill Belichick before him, that all the accomplishments in the world don’t guarantee an NFL head-coaching job. Or perhaps he’ll convince some owner to give the oldest coach ever a chance to do what he’s done three times before, and turn a franchise around.

sports.title: Luke McCaffrey knew the rules and made a heads-up play, causing a kickoff out of bounds
sports.summary: Commanders kickoff returner Luke McCaffrey made the smartest play of the game by not returning a kick in Thursday night's win over the Giants.
sports.body:
With McCaffrey back to field a Giants kickoff, the ball landed near the sideline at the 5-yard line. The kick stayed in bounds, and some returners would have grabbed the ball and started running. But McCaffrey let the ball bounce, then stepped out of bounds, and then grabbed the ball with his feet down on the sideline.

By rule, the ball is out of bounds if it touches a player who is out of bounds, even if the ball actually stays in bounds. By touching the ball while his feet were out of bounds, McCaffrey forced a kickoff out of bounds penalty on the Giants, putting the ball on the 40-yard line for the Commanders.

“I thought Luke McCaffrey made a really smart play that won’t show up on the stat sheet,” Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said. “That’s a difficult play. Is it out of bounds? Is it not? I was nervous about it, that’s one of the ones where you hold your breath.”

Every kickoff returner needs to know that rule, but knowing the rule is easier than having the quick-thinking ability to do what McCaffrey did, in the fourth quarter with the game on the line. It was among the smartest football plays you’ll see.

sports.title: Dan Quinn: We needed that, we needed every bit of it
sports.summary: After the win, the Commanders are 3-5-1, two games behind the division-leading Giants.
sports.body:
“We needed that. We needed every bit of it,” Quinn said. “This is one we had to have, and our guys make sure we have it.”

After the win, the Commanders are 3-5-1, two games behind the division-leading Giants, and the Commanders now own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants. Quinn’s team is still a long shot to win the NFC East, but given the state of that division, it’s not unreasonable to think the Commanders can compete.

And compete is what they did on Thursday night, in a game that went down to the final minute, just as Quinn said the Commanders expected.

“Going into it, we thought this is going to be all four quarters,” Quinn said. “It felt like the most adversity, but also the most belief. It was a balance of both, and we definitely needed that.”

sports.title: John Harbaugh expresses confidence in K Dominic Zvada
sports.summary: Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games.
sports.body:
While it happened in the first quarter and not on the final play, it stands out in a game that was decided by three points.

After New York’s 24-21 loss to the Commanders, Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked about his level of confidence in Zvada.

“ Yeah, we’re confident ,” Harbaugh said. “You know, you can’t — as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, I mean, start firing people left and right. Especially your kicker who’s a rookie. So I’m confident that he’s gonna become a good kicker. I mean, if at some point in time, it doesn’t happen, it doesn’t happen.

“But I’m not gonna panic, you know, halfway through the season when the guy who’s made a bunch of kicks, if that’s what you’re inferring we should be doing. So, you know, I mean, we’re just not gonna knee-jerk it like that. He’s gonna make kicks. He’s gonna make a lot of kicks, I believe in him. I think he’s really good, really talented. And we’re gonna give him an opportunity to do it. It’s up to him to do it.”

That’s a fair assessment of a player who’s still new to the NFL. But a kicker has one job. If he can’t do it (especially from distances that should be automatic), at some point tough questions need to be asked.

Basically, how much time will Zvada get before Harbaugh decides it’s not going to happen? That remains to be seen, if Zvada keeps missing kicks he should be making.

sports.title: Thursday Night Football: Stefon Diggs' late TD gives Commanders 24-21 win
sports.summary: The wide receiver caught a 32-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 57 seconds left.
sports.body:
The Commanders got the last laugh, winning 24-21 on Stefon Diggs’ 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. The Commanders are 3-5-1 and the Giants 5-3-1.

In an entertaining second half, the teams traded the lead four times.

The Giants took a 21-17 lead with 8:13 left on Isaiah Likely’s 66-yard catch-and-run.

The Giants then had back-to-back interceptions of Jayden Daniels. Safety Jevon Holland, who is having an All-Pro season, took the ball away from Chig Okonkwo at the 2-yard line with the Commanders on the Giants 24 with 5:27 left, and Ar’Darius Washington stepped in front of Okonkwo on fourth-and-2 at the Washington 45 with 2:15 left.

The Giants, though, couldn’t run out the clock, and the Commanders made the most of it. They needed only three plays to go 71 yards thanks to a questionable 33-yard pass interference penalty on Deonte Banks, who was covering Treylon Burks. Three plays later, Diggs scored.

The Giants reached the Washington 48 on their final drive, but J.J. McCarthy’s deep throw to Malik Nabers was intercepted by Rasul Douglas with 25 seconds left to end it.

The Giants outgained the Commanders 399 to 340, but missed a field goal and had two turnovers.

Daniels was 23-of-33 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. Rachaad White ran for 47 yards on 11 carries, and Diggs caught six passes for 83 yards. Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott each caught a touchdown pass.

sports.title: Aaron Donald on having no sacks: "They come in bunches"
sports.summary: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has played seven games this season.
sports.body:
“Sacks come in bunches,” Donald told reporters on Thursday. “It’s going to come. Just keep playing ball and keep finding ways to win. That’s the most important thing is winning. No pressure, I’m not worried about it. I’ve been playing football since I was five, six years old. They come in bunches. They’ll come eventually so just keep doing what I need to do to help this team. When they present themselves, hopefully hold the ball and take advantage of it.”

On Sunday, Donald finally played with Myles Garrett, the player whose arrival in June sparked Donald’s decision to return after two years of retirement. Garrett, in his first game since Week 1, had 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble.

Regardless, the Rams won, pushing themselves above .500 for the first time this year. On Sunday at Arizona, they have a chance to win their fourth in a row.

And Donald has another chance to get his first sack since he returned from retirement.

sports.title: Justin Jefferson: It's a joy to see Kirk Cousins take over as a leader
sports.summary: Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota, and perhaps no one is more excited about that than Justin Jefferson.
sports.body:
The wide receiver had career highs in catches (128) and yards (1,809) and earned the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year award in Cousins’ last full season with the Vikings in 2022.

“It’s really just going out there and just executing our plays ,” Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN. “It’s not really getting too juiced up about him being here or anybody being back there. It’s just all about understanding the plays that are being called, understanding the jobs that we have and executing our responsibilities. And just the plays that are there, and the plays that could be made, we just need to continue to just make those type of plays. And I’m pretty sure that the results would be a lot better.

“He just understands the game. He’s a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throw those type of plays, but he also doesn’t force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me.”

Jefferson said it was “a joy to hear [Cousins] just take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field.”

“He’s being vocal,” Jefferson said. “Just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he’s talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he’s just making sure that everybody’s on the same page. So it’s definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that’s pretty normal from him. So it’s definitely kind of cool him being back in that room and him taking that control.”

sports.body: Yuck. The New York Giants might be 5-2-1, but they’re leading what many see as among the worst divisions in the NFL. Tonight, they take on the 2-5-1 Washington Commanders — that’s right, a team they played to a tie earlier this season. Will there be similar “fireworks” for Thursday Night Football? It would be great if this game was exciting — and even better if it wasn’t in primetime. It’s safe to say that football fans have had their fill of these teams, of the NFC East, and the NFC in general. At least Week 10 gives us two AFC showdowns. The trouble is that the one on Monday night is about as bad as it gets. There aren’t any rooting interests here as it relates to the Buffalo Bills. You might find yourself cheering for the Commanders just to hand the Giants a loss, or at least see them make good on their horrible decisions that led to the tie in the previous matchup. Depending on how far back your Bills fandom goes, you may find it impossible rooting for an NFC East team (except when they face the New England Patriots, and probably the Kansas City Chiefs). There’s a lot of bad football being trotted out to the masses this season. but this is what you get tonight and you’re probably watching until the end. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 10 of Thursday Night Football. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.title: DeMarvion Overshown didn't know inactive players couldn't celebrate on the field
sports.summary: The Cowboys had 14 accepted penalties for 153 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts.
sports.body:
Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive and dressed in street clothes, came onto the field to celebrate after Quinnen Williams forced a Jonathan Taylor fumble that Shemar James returned to the Dallas 30. Overshown was penalized 15 yards, with referee Clay Martin saying, “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We have non-uniformed player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That’s a 15-yard penalty.”

Overshown apologized to head coach Brian Schottenheimer and his teammates.

“At the end of the day, I talked to Schotty about it,” Overshown said Thursday, via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News . “I apologized about it. It was definitely in the moment, but earlier I had said that as a defense, we’re going to start celebrating more, getting takeaways. And I was just caught in the moment. So you can laugh at it now, because we won the game, but in the moment, fourth quarter, tied ball game or close ball game, you don’t want a 15-yard penalty from a guy, especially that’s not even playing. So that’s a lesson learned.”

Overshown said he didn’t know the rule until linebacker Dee Winters started yelling at him, which should prompt questions about why Overshown didn’t know the rule. But he defended Schottenheimer and said he accepted his “butt chewing.”

“It’s not an indictment on Schotty. It’s on me as a player. I own it,” he said.

sports.body:
At least two TV markets in the state for which the team is named have passed on televising their Week 10 game against the Jaguars.

Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing explains that 506sports.com coverage map shows that the Knoxville and Chattanooga Fox affiliates will not televise the Jaguars-Titans game . Instead, Vikings-Packers will be shown in the 1:00 p.m. ET window.

It’s a preliminary map, as Lerner notes. The Fox affiliates in Knoxville and Chattanooga, the third- and fourth-largest cities in the league by way of population, could change their minds.

Making the situation even more unusual is the fact that Fox won’t get many Titans games, because they’re usually on CBS. The obvious takeaway is that the Fox affiliates in Knoxville and Chattanooga believe that more people will watch Packers-Vikings than will watch Jaguars-Titans.

It’s not personal, it’s business. And the affiliates think they’re business interests are best served by showing Packers-Vikings not Jaguars-Titans.

sports.title: Jim Harbaugh: Broncos took advantage of a loophole the NFL should not allow
sports.summary: The Chargers' head coach is not happy with the Broncos trying to renegotiate the trade for Daiyan Henley after the deadline, or with the NFL allowing it.
sports.body:
After agreeing to trade a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick for Henley, the Broncos told Chargers GM Joe Hortiz they couldn’t go through with it because Henley’s physical revealed concerns about his knee. The Broncos were still willing to trade for Henley, but wanted to give up less. Harbaugh believes physical exams should only be to determine whether or not the player is healthy, not to renegotiate trade terms.

“What happened with the trade? Here’s what I know, from talking to Joe: The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation, and we wouldn’t and we didn’t,” Harbaugh said. “In my opinion it’s one of those loopholes that the league should really look into, because it sets a bad precedent.”

Asked if it’s permitted for teams to renegotiate trades after the trade deadline, Harbaugh answered, “It shouldn’t be, but apparently it is. That’s why it’s a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that.”

Harbaugh said the Broncos offered to say Henley passed his physical, but only if the Chargers would take something less than the fifth-round pick the Broncos had agreed to.

“It’s a medical grade. It’s a pass-fail for a medical grade, and they told us they weren’t going to pass him if it’s a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon — they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a fill in the blank. I don’t know what to call that, but that’s what it is,” Harbaugh said.

Harbaugh is right that the NFL has set a bad precedent. By allowing teams to renegotiate trade terms after the deadline, the NFL is incentivizing teams to engage in chicanery on physical exams to squeeze their trade partners into taking less favorable deals. The Chargers refused to budge, but the NFL rules shouldn’t have put the Chargers in a position where they had to make that decision.

sports.title: Joey Porter Jr.: Injuries keeping me off field, not my contract situation
sports.summary: Porter missed practice again on Thursday with an ankle injury.
sports.body:
Porter did not play in last Sunday’s win over the Colts and his absence from the lineup has led some to question whether his lack of a contract extension is playing a role in keeping him on the sidelines. Porter insisted that isn’t the case.

“I don’t even know where that narrative come from,” Porter said, via Todd Archer of ESPN.com. “I get it. It’s the internet, but I really don’t pay no attention to that or really care for that. My goal is to win games and play football, and that’s what I want to do. So if there’s any chance I could get on the field, I’m going to get on the field and do what I do best.”

Porter joined the Cowboys in a late September trade with the Steelers and has appeared in four games with the team. He said it has been “definitely frustrating” to miss time when he would like to be making a strong impression on his new team and Friday’s injury report will bring more of an idea if he’ll be able to do that against the 49ers this weekend.

sports.title: Patrick Mahomes on Josh Downs: You can tell the intellect, how he can pick things up
sports.summary: The Chiefs brought in a receiver at the trading deadline, acquiring Josh Downs from the Colts.
sports.body:
Quarterback Patrick Mahomes told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that he’s excited to get going with the wideout.

“I think you can tell just the intellect and how he’s able to pick stuff up and that he’s a professional, that he knows what he’s doing and he wants to come in and just compete and to have success, and he wants to win. And so, I’m excited for that,” Mahomes said, via transcript from the team. “And then you can just see him interacting with the other receivers in the room. You can tell that there’s going to be a great cohesion there, and that’s the type of guys you want on the team, that want to compete and that want to win.”

Mahomes noted he’s impressed with the way Downs can win his one-on-one matchups.

“He runs routes really well,” Mahomes said. “He sets them up really well where he will run a route early in the game that he sets up for another one later in the game. And then he has really good feel, you can tell, obviously, playing in the system that he has, he has a lot of read-type routes, and you can tell he knows how to get himself open, settle in the right zones, and win versus man [coverage] when he can.

“And so, I think it will be an easy transition for him to kind of do that stuff in our offense. Then, with how we do things, he can play a lot of different positions as we move receivers and tight ends around.”

The quarterback also sees it as realistic for Downs to play and contribute early on in his tenure with Kansas City. While that begins with plenty of reps at practice, Mahomes and the rest of the offense can direct Downs to where he needs to be during games if necessary.

“[W]e do a great job of kind of moving guys in and out of every single position, and so guys know the entire concepts of the plays,” Mahomes said. “We’re very detailed with how we call the plays in the huddle, which will help him out a ton.

“Then when he doesn’t know, being able to talk to me in the huddle or talk to the guys as they’re breaking the huddle, and that usually helps when the guys like each other. And so, it’s good to have a guy that you can tell everybody’s going to like, and that he has his head on the right way, and he’s going to make sure that he’s going to do whatever it takes to win.”

sports.title: Jacoby Brissett: The last week has definitely been a crash course
sports.summary: Jacoby Brissett has been a member of the Ravens for less than a week, but he's set to start at quarterback in the team's game against the Chargers on Monday night.
sports.body:
The Ravens lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries in Week 8 and got the wheels moving on their trade for Brissett ahead of their loss to the Jaguars last Thursday night, but the deal didn’t become official until Friday. That left Brissett with a short window to pick up the offense for a 4-5 team that’s hoping to stay afloat in the second half of the season.

“It’s definitely been a crash course . No question,” Brissett said.

Brissett said it has “been a long, but fast, week” and said he’s confident in the work he’s done with the coaching staff to digest the offense. That work will continue — Brissett joked that the press conference was interrupting his crash course — and it will likely keep going until close to kickoff on Monday night.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets meet Sunday for another round of their twice-a-year AFC East rivalry, and recent history has been pretty kind to Buffalo. The Bills lead the all-time series 73-58, have won five straight against New York and own a 10-2 record against the Jets since 2020. Buffalo has also kept New York out of the end zone on its opening drive in each of their last 25 meetings. It’s been a while since the Jets have given Bills fans much reason to worry. Of course, when two teams have been playing each other twice a year for decades, there’s only so much history we can dig up before we start telling the same stories. And while we’re always happy to revisit a good Bills win, even our Time Capsule could use a change of scenery. Head coach Aaron Glenn, defensive coordinator Brian Duker and offensive coordinator Frank Reich all have some history with Buffalo. They’ve faced Allen, coached against the Bills and, in Reich’s case, even worn a Buffalo uniform. Glenn already has a season with the Jets under his belt, while Duker and Reich are getting their first taste of this rivalry from New York’s sideline. But none of them is a stranger to Buffalo, and their previous encounters give us a few interesting games to revisit. _____________________________________________________________________________ Aaron Glenn has seen plenty of Josh Allen Aaron Glenn is in his second season as the Jets’ head coach, but his history with Josh Allen goes back to his four seasons as defensive coordinator for the Detroit Lions. And if Glenn was hoping a change of teams would make Allen any easier to deal with, the results so far haven’t offered much encouragement. Up front, Hooker is at his best in a deep-coverage role. Of course, in the modern NFL, he’s played everywhere in the back seven. But the film and numbers suggest he’s the most impactful when he can process route concepts, check the quarterback, and range to the football. On 1,172 snaps across the 2020 and 2021 campaigns — his second and third in the NFL — Hooker played 717 snaps as a free safety (61.1%) and rewarded the Titans with a total of five interceptions and 12 pass breakups in 28 games. In those years, Hooker averaged just under 42 snaps per contest. In 2024, when Hooker had five interceptions, he aligned at free safety on 55.9% of his snaps. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills made one move before the trade deadline, a reasonable transaction with the Tennessee Titans to acquire safety Amani Hooker. The move has been widely regarded as a wise one by the Bills. Needing help on a defense that seems destined to eventually cost Buffalo a game, pretty much everyone is of the belief that Hooker will help cover up some flaws with solid defensive back play. Well I have one thing to say to that… Yeah, pretty much. This is a case of everyone being right. I’ll give you my thoughts on the matter with a short highlight reel but this was a great move by Buffalo. Some film and opinions [Media: https://twitter.com/Kuebiko_Kami/status/2120731699164139571?a=wdetkgsxvccD9wqT5yw&s=20] What you have there for the video is Amani Hooker’s five interceptions this year. Does that seem like a lot of interceptions in what amounts to half a season? Because it is. Hooker is tied with Green Bay’s Xavier Mckinney for the lead league with that five. In reality though, Hooker should be considered the interception leader so far in 2026. McKinney’s five interceptions come from nine games, and if you like granular assessment he’s played on 604 snaps. That means he has one interception every 121-ish plays. Hooker was out for one game with a concussion and Tennessee was on their bye this week. He’s appeared in just 495 snaps, for an interception rate of one every 99 plays. In the film above, I went with just the interceptions primarily because they’re fun, but there’s plenty to see on them as well. Hooker’s anticipation and ability to read the quarterback is excellent. Over his career that’s led to variable interception totals and being transparent here, 2026 has already tied his career high, achieved in 2024. So really, the ballhawk thing is hopefully a “from now on” kinda deal. I don’t mean to suggest he’s been poor at it, only that this year is very good even for Hooker. The traits that have led to it in 2026 are good signs for all facets of safety play though. Hooker is a heads up defensive back that processes the game with speed and gets into the mix quickly. That’s been interceptions this year, but it also means he’s there for tackles and other support. I don’t want to oversell him either. It’s a question that folds in opportunity cost amongst all potential other maneuvers. In this author’s opinion, the Hooker transaction is both good and optimal. sports.body: It’s sounding more and more like new Buffalo Bills safety Amani Hooker could suit up to play in Week 10 against the New York Jets, at least if we’re to read the tea leaves from head coach Joe Brady’s latest media session. Brady pointed to Hooker’s status as a “savvy” and “cerebral” eight-year NFL veteran who oozes “football intelligence” with a ton of experience to boot. Brady said that “(s)ometimes it’s just about learning the terminology, and it might of meant this in one place, but now it’s this — and I think these guys usually pick it up at a fast rate.” As such, Brady and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard aren’t going to hurry Hooker, nor ask him to do anything he’s not prepared to tackle within Buffalo’s scheme, noting “we’ll take it day by day and see how much he can process, and how fast he can and what he can handle to be able to go out there on the road and be able to communicate — whatever he can handle, we’ll ask him to do that.” It’s undoubtedly a short turnaround for Hooker to potentially suit up and play for his new team. Fortunately, he was on a bye this past week with his old team, the Tennessee Titans. However, arriving on Wednesday and having to navigate everything that comes with packing up and moving to a new city is no small feat for an NFL player. For his part, Hooker sounds ready to go, and very excited, admitting that he’s “on social media, so I hear all the rumors,” which means he probably had a feeling something was brewing. When asked about the challenge of changing teams midseason, Hooker didn’t hesitate in stepping up to the plate, saying “I pride myself on being a pro and being ready when my name is called no matter what.” His plan? Hooker will soak up all he can with his coaches this week, putting in “a little overtime this week and get up to speed on the style of play we want here, and just deliver.” When asked just how different is Leonhard’s scheme is, Hooker simply said that “at the end of the day, it’s football. Every team runs Cover 4. Every team runs Cover 2, and Cover 3. So, it’s really just about terminology, and what they call different things , and how they play certain looks. sports.body: The Jets recently signed former Steelers defensive lineman Isaiahh Loudermilk to their practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 29-year old Loudermilk is listed at 6’7” and 293 pounds and was a fifth round pick out of Wisconsin in 2021. He has started seven games in his NFL career, with 63 tackles, six passes defensed and one sack. Background Loudermilk was a three-star high school recruit despite only having played 8-man football in a small town. He ended up going to Wisconsin, where he redshirted his first season in 2016, but then became a useful player over the next few years. In 2017, Loudermilk had six tackles in 11 games in a reserve role, adding 1.5 sacks and a pass defensed. He started the first six games of his career in 2018 and ended up with 15 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, three passes defensed and a sack in nine games. In 2019, he started all 14 games and had his most productive season with 24 tackles, five tackles for loss, three sacks, five pass breakups and two forced fumbles. However, Loudermilk got all Big-10 recognition for the only time in his final season as he was named as a third-teamer by the media and an honorable mention by the coaches. In just six games during the pandemic-shortened 2020 season, he had 13 tackles and two sacks. After not being invited to the scouting combine, Loudermilk played in the East-West Shrine Bowl and was eventually drafted by the Steelers in the fifth round of the 2021 draft. As a rookie, he started two games and ended up with 23 tackles, a sack and two pass breakups in 15 appearances. In 2022, Loudermilk started three times but had just seven tackles and a tackle for loss in 11 games overall. He played in 16 games in both 2023 and 2024 but did not start a game during that time. He ended up with 33 tackles, three passes defensed and a quarterback hit over the two seasons. 2025 saw Loudermilk start the first two games, although he didn’t generate any statistics. An injury in the second game sidelined him for the rest of the season. He was almost ready to return for the postseason but wasn’t cleared in time. Loudermilk signed for the Vikings in the offseason but failed to make their roster and was eventually added to the Jets’ practice squad last month.
